title: Receptive Field
interviewAnswer: A unit’s receptive field is the input region that can influence it. Deeper layers, larger kernels, stride and dilation increase receptive field and therefore spatial context.
why: Receptive field explains how CNN features gather spatial context and why architecture choices affect fine details versus global structure.
intuition: A feature in a deep layer “sees” a region of the original image. Deeper layers, larger kernels, stride and dilation increase that region.
deepDive: Theoretical receptive field accumulates through layers, but the effective receptive field may be smaller/nonuniform. Stride/pooling enlarge field faster while reducing spatial resolution. Dilation enlarges context without the same parameter count. For segmentation/reconstruction, balancing global context with local detail motivates skip connections and multi-scale architectures.
workedExample: Two stacked 3×3 stride-1 convolutions give a 5×5 theoretical receptive field; adding a stride-2 layer makes each subsequent feature cover input positions farther apart.
commonMistakes: Equating receptive field with kernel size of one layer.
Assuming every pixel inside the theoretical field contributes equally.
Increasing stride without considering lost detail.
followUps: How does dilation affect receptive field?
production: For large images/3D patches, receptive field determines whether the model has enough contextual information; patch sizes and tiling overlap must match it.
